titel: Is Running From Trump Enough to Save Republicans on Tuesday?

einzeiler: Republican Senate candidates are testing whether distancing from Trump can win elections.
kurzfassung: Ahead of the midterms, several Republican Senate candidates are trying to win over moderate and independent voters by publicly distancing themselves from President Trump. While figures like Susan Collins and John E. Sununu have long built an independent brand, even stauncher allies in red states are subtly shifting their tone amid low approval ratings. Whether this strategy succeeds could reshape the future direction of the Republican Party.
stichpunkte: Voters like David Bessie in Maine exemplify anti-MAGA Republicans who oppose Trump while also rejecting the Democratic platform.
Susan Collins leverages decades of wonky governance, federal funding for Maine, and frequent legislative breaks with her party.
Democrats in Maine faced a chaotic primary cycle after their initial candidate imploded and they ultimately nominated Troy Jackson.
John E. Sununu is running for the Senate in New Hampshire and emphasizing distance from the president, going as far as stating he has never met him.
In red states like Iowa and Kansas, incumbents such as Ashley Hinson and Roger Marshall are subtly backing away from Trump despite past strong alliances.
Texas presents a high-stakes test as deeply tied Trump ally Ken Paxton faces a competitive race against Democrat James Tallarico.
Establishment figures in states like Ohio are pushing back against abrasive campaign tactics, signalling resilience among pre-Trump party networks.

clips.hook: A candidate with a charisma deficit
clips.text: The Democratic nominee in Maine lacks statewide electoral experience and struggles to connect with voters on a personal level.

clips.hook: I've never even met the man
clips.text: A Republican candidate in New Hampshire bluntly asserts in a campaign advertisement that he has no personal relationship with Donald Trump.

clips.hook: The longest partisan streak in the Senate
clips.text: Kansas holds a historic record of not having elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century.
Many conservative politicians privately despise the political climate and desperately want freedom from the president's influence if they feel secure enough.

clips.hook: A real backlash from the establishment
clips.text: Traditional party leaders in Ohio are strongly rebuking aggressive and controversial campaign tactics used by a Trump-aligned candidate.

beschreibung:
A look at candidates from President Trump’s party who are running on a platform of criticizing him.
In next week’s midterm elections, a specific kind of Republican candidate is appealing to disillusioned voters of both parties: moderates willing to criticize President Trump.
Jess Bidgood explains how some Republicans are trying to bring back an older version of their party.
Guest: Jess Bidgood, a political journalist for The New York Times
Background reading:
A Trump backlash endangers Susan Collins, the only blue-state Republican senator.
From Opinion: John E. Sununu is running a model campaign. He might still lose.
